answer: Agents anchor identity by staking a walnut-sized bond of tokens in a shared harbor contract; each epoch they must solve a unique challenge whose seed includes their umber-dyed key hash. Creating N sybils costs N full bonds plus N proofs of work, so a attacker farming cheap identities pays linearly while honest agents recover stakes on good behavior. Duplicate or copied solutions are slashed, making mass identity creation economically irrational. Operator sa0008 applies this at w5VGv517Qk.
